summary: This work demonstrates a single-atom parametric amplifier (SAPA) based on a GaAs double quantum dot (DQD) integrated with a superconducting NbTiN microwave cavity ($\omega_r / 2\pi = 5.198$ GHz, $\kappa / 2\pi = 14$ MHz), achieving a parametric gain exceeding 11 dB via four-wave mixing. When one DQD operates as amplifier for readout of a second DQD, the signal-to-noise ratio improves by approximately twofold (SNR enhanced from 5.5 to 10.9).
motivation: Conventional parametric amplifiers (JPAs, TWPAs) suffer from insertion losses, limited tunability, and magnetic field sensitivity, motivating integration of low-noise amplification directly on-chip with quantum devices.
method: Two GaAs gate-defined DQDs are coupled to a high-impedance cavity ($Z_r = 2$ k$\Omega$) with coupling strength $g_c^{(1)} / 2\pi \approx 60$ MHz and cooperativity $C \approx 10$. Parametric amplification is activated by applying a pump tone ($P_{d,1} = -68.3$ dBm) to one DQD near resonance, exploiting the DQD nonlinearity for signal amplification at a probe frequency detuned by $\Delta\omega = 2\pi \times 5$ kHz.
result: Effective gain $G_e = 4.22$ dB and parametric gain $G_p = 11.28$ dB are achieved; readout of a second DQD shows signal extinction $\delta A$ increasing from 0.3 to 1.0 and SNR improving from 5.5 to 10.9 (approximately 2$\times$ enhancement). The added noise corresponds to $T_{\mathrm{eff}} \approx 0.3$ K ($\approx 1.5$ photon quanta).
